name: Hack Canada
description: A student hackathon bringing together hackers from universities across Canada, with travel reimbursement and over $10K in prizes. Free to attend for high school and university students. The 2026 edition was held in Waterloo; 2027 moves to the University of Toronto.

name: Hackfest CTF
description: 24-hour on-site capture-the-flag competition run during Hackfest, Canada's largest bilingual hacking and cybersecurity event; requires a Hackfest ticket plus a CTF ticket.

name: Capital Hacks
description: Three-day student hackathon at Sacramento State (formerly Hornet Hacks) run by the Carlsen Center for Innovation & Entrepreneurship and ACM Sac State, with civic/govtech, health, sustainability and wildcard tracks and $3,500 in cash prizes.

name: SIGCSE TS
audience: computer science educators, researchers, graduate students
description: ACM SIGCSE Technical Symposium, the largest computing-education conference: papers, panels, posters, Nifty Assignments, demos and an exhibit hall for CS educators.

name: California Government Technology Summit
audience: state and local government IT leaders, public-sector technologists, industry partners
description: One-day Government Technology summit for California state and local government on AI, cybersecurity, data governance and digital service delivery, with the State CIO among the keynotes.

name: MadHacks
description: UW-Madison's long-running 24-hour student hackathon, one of the largest in the Midwest, with mentorship, workshops, meals and prizes.

name: Israel Tech Week
description: Five-day programme in Miami connecting Israeli startups with U.S. investors and corporates: sector days on defense, cybersecurity, AI, fintech and healthtech, a startup showcase and a VC and investors summit.

name: HackMiami
description: South Florida's hacker conference: four days of paid security trainings followed by a two-track talks day.

name: Venture Madness
audience: tech founders, accredited investors, venture capital and private equity firms
description: One-day conference and expo where Arizona's most promising tech startups pitch to investors, run by Invest Southwest since 1992.

name: Venture Café Phoenix Thursday Gathering
description: Free weekly Thursday-evening gathering at the Phoenix Bioscience Core with mentor hours, workshops and talks on startups, AI and innovation, followed by networking.

name: Calgary Innovation Week
venue: Platform Innovation Centre (HQ) and venues across Calgary
audience: founders, investors, tech workers, students, community
description: Calgary's city-wide week of tech, innovation and entrepreneurship events, run by Platform Calgary with main-stage sessions at the Platform Innovation Centre and community-hosted offsite events; most sessions are free via its Luma calendar and the week closes with Calgary Launch Party.

name: Calgary Launch Party
description: Calgary's annual startup showcase since 2010, where the year's Top 10 early-stage Calgary startups, chosen by community nomination and expert review, demo their products on the closing night of Calgary Innovation Week.

name: Future Summit
description: One-day innovation summit in Calgary convening investors, entrepreneurs, government and industry leaders on the future of technology, AI and infrastructure.

name: CyberSci Calgary Regional
description: Calgary regional of Canada's Cyber Security Challenge: a one-day in-person capture-the-flag for post-secondary student teams, with sponsor interviews in the afternoon; winners advance to the National Finals in Ottawa.

name: Global Game Jam YYC
audience: game developers, artists, musicians, students, beginners
description: The Calgary Game Developers Association's in-person Global Game Jam site: a beginner-friendly weekend making games with meals, judges, prizes and a public playtest showcase.

name: Global Entrepreneurship Week Kansas City
audience: entrepreneurs, founders, small business owners, investors, students
description: Kansas City's Global Entrepreneurship Week at Union Station, run by KCSourceLink: expert-led sessions, speakers, a maker fair, an ecosystem-builder day and youth programming for founders at every stage.

name: Pipeline Innovators Pitch Showcase
venue: Union Station Planetarium, 30 W Pershing Road
description: Pipeline Entrepreneurs' annual pitch day, where the year's Fellows and Pathfinders, high-growth founders from across the Midwest, pitch to a national judging panel, followed in the evening by the Innovators Gala.

name: Waterloo Tech Week
description: A decentralized week of independently hosted talks, demos, panels, meetups and pitch events celebrating Waterloo's tech community, organised by the Hack the North team in the run-up to the hackathon.

name: Velocity Pitch Competition
venue: Science Teaching Complex, University of Waterloo
audience: University of Waterloo student founders, investors, community
description: Velocity's pitch competition for University of Waterloo student-led startups, running since 2011; the 2026 edition put teams through two-minute, no-slide pitches before 100 judges for a $5,000 top prize.

name: Impact Venture Demo Day
venue: Davidson Winter Garden, Ross School of Business
description: University of Michigan-wide demo day where 25+ student ventures from the Ross Impact Studio and partner programs show live prototypes in tech for good, health, education, climate and fintech to investors and the public.

name: MidwestCon
venue: 1819 Innovation Hub and venues across Cincinnati
description: Four-day AI and technology conference week in Cincinnati, centred on UC's 1819 Innovation Hub, combining policy and AI sessions, a hackathon, an art-and-AI showcase and partner events.

name: Capture Ohio: OCRI Statewide CTF
venue: Clifton Court Hall, University of Cincinnati
description: The Ohio Cyber Range Institute's annual one-day statewide capture-the-flag for student teams of three to five, hosted in person at the University of Cincinnati with partner campuses across Ohio joining the same day.

name: Ray Summit
audience: ML engineers, AI infrastructure and platform teams, researchers
description: Anyscale's three-day conference for the Ray open-source community: a hands-on training day followed by two days of keynotes and production talks on model training, multimodal data, RL and AI infrastructure, co-located with the vLLM Conference.

name: Commit Your Code
description: Community-built two-day developer conference in Dallas-Fort Worth from Dallas Software Developers: six technical tracks, Day 0 community events and a free livestream, with a $40 in-person ticket and all net ticket revenue donated to charity.

name: Midwest Tech Conference
audience: developers and tech enthusiasts, students free
description: Volunteer-run one-day community tech conference in mid-Missouri with talks and workshops for enthusiasts to experts; $10 tickets and free for students.

name: MAIS Hacks
description: McGill Artificial Intelligence Society's annual fall 48-hour AI hackathon at McGill, with workshops, mentoring and networking with Montreal researchers and companies.

name: CGU Hacks
description: Two-day transdisciplinary hackathon run by CGU's AI for Humanity Lab and CISAT, with workshops, mentoring and tracks in AI, GeoAI, cybersecurity and UI/UX, focused on ethical, human-centred innovation.

name: CUSEC
audience: university and college software engineering and computer science students
description: Canada's longest-running student-led software engineering conference: three days of talks, hands-on workshops, a sponsor career fair and evening socials, with school delegations from across the country.

name: QCon AI New York
audience: senior software engineers, architects, engineering leaders running AI in production
description: Two-day practitioner conference from the QCon organisers on running AI systems in production: agents, evals, AI code review, token costs and guardrails, with talks from senior engineers at companies such as LinkedIn, Netflix and DoorDash.

name: DesignCon
audience: hardware, chip, board and system design engineers
description: Engineering conference and expo for chip, board and system design, covering signal and power integrity, high-speed interconnects and test, with a technical programme and an exhibit hall.

name: DeisHacks
description: Brandeis University's 48-hour social-good hackathon, where student teams from every major build prototypes for challenges set by local nonprofit partners.

name: Global Power Platform Bootcamp Calgary
audience: Power Platform makers, developers, business analysts, IT professionals
description: Free one-day community-run Calgary stop of the worldwide Global Power Platform Bootcamp, with hands-on sessions and labs on Power Apps, Power Automate, Copilot and agents.

name: Socratica
audience: makers, engineers, founders, researchers, designers, students
description: Weekly Sunday-morning co-working session run by an open collective of makers, engineers, founders and artists: introductions, two focused work blocks on personal projects, then open demos. Runs in term-length seasons (Fall, Winter, Spring) with occasional weeknight and showcase events; RSVP on Wygo.
